question: what is this company worth, and what does the price already assume?

value_range.reading: Python's three scenarios put the value per share between {valuation.value_range_per_share.low} in the bear case and {valuation.value_range_per_share.high} in the bull case, with the base case, my best reading rather than a midpoint, at {valuation.scenarios.base.value_per_share}. Behind those sit enterprise values of {valuation.scenarios.bear.enterprise_value}, {valuation.scenarios.base.enterprise_value} and {valuation.scenarios.bull.enterprise_value}; net debt of {valuation.scenarios.base.net_debt} and the operating lease liability of {valuation.scenarios.base.operating_lease_liability} come off each to give equity values of {valuation.scenarios.bear.equity_value}, {valuation.scenarios.base.equity_value} and {valuation.scenarios.bull.equity_value}, spread over diluted shares of {valuation.scenarios.base.diluted_shares}. All three are discounted at a WACC of {valuation.wacc|pct}, which is high because the cost of equity of {cost_of_capital.cost_of_equity|pct} rests on a beta of {cost_of_capital.beta} over a risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct}; at that rate distant cash flows count for little, and in the base case the terminal value contributes {valuation.scenarios.base.terminal_value_present} of enterprise value against {valuation.scenarios.base.explicit_present} from the ten explicit years. The range is wide because the scenarios disagree about how much of the current upcycle is structural. The bear starts growth at {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct} and lets the operating margin fade to {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct} by year ten, near the fiscal 2021 and fiscal 2022 upcycle margins; the bull starts at {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct} and holds a year-ten margin of {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}, about the trailing record of {ratios.profitability.operating_margin|pct}. Year-ten revenue accordingly runs from {valuation.scenarios.bear.years.9.revenue} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.years.9.revenue}, against trailing revenue of {terms.trailing_four_quarters.revenue}. The base takes year-one growth of {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct}, below the trailing {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct} and above the three-year compound {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}, and a margin fading from {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_one|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}, which is still above every year on record before the trailing one.

price_position.reading: The price at the cutoff, {valuation.price_at_cutoff}, is {valuation.price_position}: above the bull case's {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share} and a multiple of the base case's {valuation.scenarios.base.value_per_share}. At that price the market value of equity is {cost_of_capital.market_value_of_equity}, against a bull-case equity value of {valuation.scenarios.bull.equity_value}. The bull case is not a timid one. It starts growth at {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct}, above the trailing year's {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, itself a fifty-three-week year with pricing gains inside it; it holds the year-ten operating margin at {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}, about the best year on record and far above the three-year average of {earnings_versus_cash.history.operating_margin_three_year_average|pct}; it reinvests only {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.reinvestment_rate_year_ten|pct} of after-tax operating income at the steady state; and its terminal growth of {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.terminal_growth|pct} sits just under the risk-free cap of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct}. That the price clears even this says the price rests on something none of the three scenarios contains: revenue compounding faster than the bull's fading path, margins above the record held for a decade, a discount rate well below the beta-driven {valuation.wacc|pct}, or some combination. The sensitivity grid shows that the discount rate alone, within the tested step, does not close the gap: at a WACC of {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.1.wacc|pct} the base case is worth {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.1.value_per_share}. The accounting analysis adds nothing in the price's favour: its findings, receivables outrunning revenue, a supplier finance programme inside payables, operating cash flow lifted by unpaid taxes and settlements, and grants credited against cost, all point to reported earnings and cash sitting at or a little above their economic level, not below it.

market_implied_growth.reading: The reverse DCF finds the constant revenue growth at which the base case is worth the price: {valuation.reverse_dcf.value|pct} every year for ten years, holding {valuation.reverse_dcf.held}. That is not a fading path like my scenarios but the same rate held for the whole decade. Against the company's own record it is above the trailing year's {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, which had an extra week and which management attributes partly to pricing actions rather than volume; close to the prior year's {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.revenue_growth|pct}; about double the three-year compound rate of {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}; and set against a history in which revenue fell {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.3.revenue_growth|pct} in fiscal 2023 and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.revenue_growth|pct} in fiscal 2024. From the fiscal 2022 revenue of {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.4.revenue} to the trailing {terms.trailing_four_quarters.revenue}, the record across a full cycle compounds at a small fraction of the implied rate. The company's guidance covers one quarter: it guides revenue for the first quarter of the new fiscal year above the fourth quarter's {ratios.growth.revenue.this_quarter}, which itself grew {ratios.growth.revenue.year_over_year|pct} on the year-ago quarter and {ratios.growth.revenue.quarter_over_quarter|pct} sequentially, and the chief executive says the momentum continues into the coming year. That is consistent with the near-term part of the base case, not with a decade at the implied rate; the MD&A claims greater visibility into demand from pricing strategy, supply discipline and long-term customer engagements, and nothing more. The implied rate also carries the base margin path, which fades from {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_one|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.base.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}. A reader who held the bull's margins instead would need less growth, but the bull scenario, which does exactly that and starts growth at {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct}, still values the share at {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share}, below the price.

most_sensitive.assumption: revenue growth over the ten explicit years
most_sensitive.reading: The scenario spread is the widest thing the calculator prints: value per share runs from {valuation.scenarios.bear.value_per_share} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share} as year-one growth moves from {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct} and year-ten revenue from {valuation.scenarios.bear.years.9.revenue} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.years.9.revenue}. That span is many times wider than the whole sensitivity grid, whose corners are {valuation.sensitivity.grid.2.0.value_per_share} and {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.2.value_per_share}. The margin path moves with growth in each scenario, the year-ten margin from {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct} to {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.operating_margin_year_ten|pct}, and compounds the effect, so the spread does not separate the two cleanly; but the reverse DCF, which holds the base margins and varies growth alone, shows growth is the lever the price is pulling, at {valuation.reverse_dcf.value|pct} held constant for ten years. Growth is also the assumption with the weakest anchor in the record: the last two years grew {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.1.revenue_growth|pct} and {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}, the two before them fell {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.3.revenue_growth|pct} and {earnings_versus_cash.history.years.2.revenue_growth|pct}, and the accounting analysis reads part of the latest year's growth as price rather than volume and part as an extra week.

most_sensitive.assumption: the discount rate, which is almost entirely a beta-driven cost of equity
most_sensitive.reading: Within the grid, one point of WACC moves the base value from {valuation.sensitivity.grid.1.1.value_per_share} to {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.1.value_per_share} at {valuation.sensitivity.grid.0.1.wacc|pct} and to {valuation.sensitivity.grid.2.1.value_per_share} at {valuation.sensitivity.grid.2.1.wacc|pct}, whereas half a point of terminal growth moves it only to {valuation.sensitivity.grid.1.0.value_per_share} at {valuation.sensitivity.grid.1.0.terminal_growth|pct} and {valuation.sensitivity.grid.1.2.value_per_share} at {valuation.sensitivity.grid.1.2.terminal_growth|pct}; of the two the grid varies, the discount rate is the stronger, and terminal growth, capped at the risk-free rate of {cost_of_capital.risk_free_rate|pct}, is the weakest of the tested assumptions. The discount rate matters more than the grid's single step shows. The WACC of {valuation.wacc|pct} is almost entirely the cost of equity of {cost_of_capital.cost_of_equity|pct}, since equity is {cost_of_capital.weights.equity|pct} of the capital structure at the cutoff price, and that cost of equity is the risk-free rate plus a beta of {cost_of_capital.beta}, measured against SPY over the {market.beta.trading_days} trading days before the cutoff, times a premium of {cost_of_capital.equity_risk_premium|pct}. A reader who took a lower beta would discount every year's cash flow less and reach a higher value in every scenario; the grid does not extend far enough to say where the price would be met, and I do not estimate it.

accounting_adjustments.reading: One adjustment was carried from the accounting analysis: {valuation.accounting_adjustments.each.0.name}, the confirmed obligation that rose from {terms.balances_a_year_earlier.supplier_finance_obligation} to {terms.balances_now.supplier_finance_obligation} inside accounts payable while the MD&A's explanation of the payables rise named capital expenditure and not the programme. It applies to cash flow and is treated as non-recurring; Python applied it as {valuation.accounting_adjustments.each.0.mechanism}. It moved the base value per share by {valuation.accounting_adjustments.each.0.moved_per_share}, from {valuation.accounting_adjustments.base_value_per_share} to {valuation.accounting_adjustments.all_together.value_per_share}, which is small against the base value and negligible against the distance between the range and the price of {valuation.price_at_cutoff}. Two further findings in the accounting analysis carry no calculator field and so were not adjusted: operating cash flow lifted by accrued but unpaid taxes and legal settlements, and government grants credited against cost of revenue that are conditional and can be recaptured. Both would point the same way as the carried adjustment, toward a lower value, so their omission does not bear on the finding that the price sits above the range. The quality-adjusted free cash flow of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_quality_adjusted}, which already deducts share-based compensation and the same supplier finance balance, sits below the simple figure of {free_cash_flow.free_cash_flow_simple} for the same reasons.

summary_ko.value_range: 세 시나리오로 계산한 주당 가치는 약세 {valuation.value_range_per_share.low}달러에서 강세 {valuation.value_range_per_share.high}달러 사이이며, 제 최선의 읽기인 기본 시나리오는 {valuation.scenarios.base.value_per_share}달러입니다. 할인율이 {valuation.wacc|pct}로 높아 먼 미래의 현금흐름이 크게 눌리고, 범위가 넓은 것은 지금의 호황 중 얼마가 구조적인지를 두고 시나리오마다 판단이 크게 다르기 때문입니다.
summary_ko.price_position: 기준일 주가 {valuation.price_at_cutoff}달러는 세 시나리오의 범위 위에 있으며, 강세 시나리오의 {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share}달러보다도 높습니다. 따라서 주가는 세 시나리오 어디에도 없는 가정, 곧 강세보다 빠른 성장이나 기록적 마진의 십 년 유지, 혹은 베타에 기댄 {valuation.wacc|pct}보다 훨씬 낮은 할인율을 이미 전제하고 있습니다.
summary_ko.market_implied_growth: 역산 DCF에 따르면 기본 시나리오의 마진과 재투자율을 그대로 두고 주가에 이르려면 매출이 십 년 동안 매년 {valuation.reverse_dcf.value|pct}씩 꾸준히 성장해야 합니다. 이는 오십삼 주짜리였던 직전 연도의 {ratios.growth.revenue.trailing_four_quarters|pct}보다 높고 삼 년 복합성장률 {earnings_versus_cash.history.revenue_growth_three_year_compound|pct}의 약 두 배이며, 회사의 가이던스는 다음 한 분기만을 제시합니다.
summary_ko.most_sensitive: 가치를 가장 크게 움직이는 가정은 향후 십 년의 매출 성장 경로로, 첫해 성장률이 {valuation.scenarios.bear.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct}에서 {valuation.scenarios.bull.drivers.revenue_growth_year_one|pct}로 바뀌면 주당 가치가 {valuation.scenarios.bear.value_per_share}달러에서 {valuation.scenarios.bull.value_per_share}달러로 벌어집니다. 그다음은 할인율로, 민감도 표에서 WACC 일 퍼센트포인트 변화가 영구성장률 영점오 퍼센트포인트 변화보다 가치를 더 크게 움직이며, 그 할인율은 베타 {cost_of_capital.beta}에 기대고 있습니다.
summary_ko.accounting_adjustments: 회계 분석에서 넘어온 조정은 매입채무 안에 든 공급망금융 채무 {terms.balances_now.supplier_finance_obligation} 하나이며, 일회성 차감으로 기본 시나리오 주당 가치를 {valuation.accounting_adjustments.each.0.moved_per_share}달러만큼 움직여 {valuation.accounting_adjustments.base_value_per_share}달러에서 {valuation.accounting_adjustments.all_together.value_per_share}달러가 되었습니다. 기본 가치에 비해 작고, 범위와 주가 사이의 간격에 비하면 무시할 만한 크기입니다.

limits: This valuation is a set of stated assumptions run through a stated formula. It states no recommendation to trade, and a different reader choosing different drivers would reach a different value.
